analyst_view.overall: Early view: Palace are bottom and may have a new manager by then, with one report saying Pierre Sage is on the brink and Thomas Frank is favourite to replace him. Jean-Philippe Mateta's three-match ban covers this game too. Hull are 13th with three draws in their last five and a long injury list.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean slightly lower: Palace have scored once in four league games and will still be without Mateta, while Hull have drawn three of their last five and held Arsenal to a single goal.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 5.5 for Palace. Palace at home should push, and Hull's deep defending concedes corners, so I keep the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards, 2.6 of them Hull's. I lean higher: Hull had six names in the book at Arsenal, and a home game for a bottom side under this much pressure adds tension. Five bookings would not surprise me.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots, 15.7 of them Palace's. I lean lower: Palace's attack without Mateta and Ismaila Sarr has barely produced, and Hull's block limited Arsenal to one goal.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. I lean lower for the same reasons: Palace lack a reliable finisher with Mateta banned, and Hull's deep defending blocks a lot of efforts.
